//: Shared editor settings. rust-analyzer runs its own cargo builds; by default they contend with terminal builds on the target/ lock and roughly double build times on this dependency graph. targetDir gives it a private target/ so the two never collide.
//constrained-machines: On a low-core host you can also disable these two. They cut CPU further, at the cost of worse IDE analysis: without proc-macro expansion the serde/schemars derives do not resolve and the editor shows errors that are not real. Leave them on unless builds are genuinely painful.
